verse.text: Ah, Sovereign LORD, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.

reflection.scripture: Ah, Sovereign LORD, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
reflection.observation: Jeremiah is speaking to God at a time when Jerusalem is under siege and the future looks bleak. Despite the chaos around him, Jeremiah's prayer begins with a declaration of God's sovereignty and creative power. He reminds himself that the same God who spoke galaxies into existence with an outstretched arm is the same God he is praying to. The phrase "Nothing is too hard for you" isn't wishful thinking — it's a theological anchor. Jeremiah is about to ask God for something that seems impossible (buying a field in a warzone as a sign of future hope), and he starts by grounding his request in God's unlimited capability.
reflection.application: When life feels like a siege — when finances, relationships, or circumstances seem impossible — our first move should be the same as Jeremiah's: remind ourselves who God is before we ask Him for what we need. The size of our problem doesn't change the size of our God. What's one area in your life where you've been treating God as if your situation is "too hard" for Him? Take a moment to declare His power over that situation today, not as a magic formula, but as an act of realignment.
reflection.prayer: Sovereign LORD, You made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. I declare that nothing is too hard for You — not my circumstances, not my struggles, not my unanswered questions. Help me to start my prayers with who You are, not just what I need. Align my heart with Your unlimited capability. In Jesus' name, Amen.
